notes: Every sizeBytes and sha256 was computed from the artifact actually downloaded and used to run the measured benchmark. Verify the hash after download and refuse to install on mismatch.

All URLs resolve through Zscaler TLS inspection using the Windows certificate store. curl.exe and Invoke-WebRequest both work; pip/certifi-based tooling does not, which is why there is no Python anywhere in this stack.
Everything is user-scope. No component requires admin rights, registry writes, or a Visual C++ redistributable.
components[].required = false are optional alternates. A minimal working install needs only the required ones.
Extraction paths in extract[].to are relative to the install root and use forward slashes. They target the INSTALLED layout: bin/{whisper,sherpa,ffmpeg}/ for executables and models/ for weights.

Track A's development tree uses vendor/{whisper,sherpa,ffmpeg}/ and vendor/models/ instead. Transcribe.ps1 resolves either layout at runtime relative to its own location, so the installer does not need to rewrite app/config.default.json.

NOT EVERY COMPONENT IS DOWNLOADED. The DEFAULT speech model is DERIVED at install time - see derivedComponents[] - because it is not published anywhere. Everything the installer puts on disk is still covered by a pinned SHA-256: downloaded components by their own hash, the derived one by the hashes of the two verified inputs it is produced from plus its own pinned output hash.

DO NOT take a HuggingFace ETag as the content SHA-256. MEASURED 2026-08-27: a HEAD on huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin returns ETag 5a4b65b0...42ad, while the file's actual SHA-256 is 1fc70f77...bc69. The ETag is the CDN's entity tag on that pop, not the LFS oid, and there is no X-Linked-Etag on the response to fall back to. The authoritative value is lfs.oid from https://huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>/tree/main?recursive=true, which was cross-checked here against three files whose hashes came from real downloads (large-v3-turbo-q5_0, small-q5_1, small.en-q8_0) and agreed with all three.

components[].installTimeOnly = true means the component is an install-time INPUT, not a shipped artefact: it is downloaded, verified, consumed, and then deleted from the install tree. It is deliberately NOT recorded in install-manifest.json files[], because it is not there when the install finishes.

installLayout.bin/whisper: whisper-cli.exe, whisper-quantize.exe, plus whisper/ggml DLLs (all ggml-cpu-* variants). whisper-quantize.exe has to live in THIS directory, beside those DLLs: MEASURED, with them absent it exits 53 having printed nothing at all, which is indistinguishable from success if you only check for output.
installLayout.models: ggml-*.bin speech models and ggml-silero-*.bin VAD model.

_sizeNote: totalAllBytes is DOWNLOAD volume and is now much larger than totalInstalledBytes. That is new and it is the point: 1624555275 of the download is the f16 source for the derived default model, and it never survives the install. Net of it, downloads are 1234248203. totalInstalledBytes was MEASURED on a clean install into an empty root on 2026-08-27 - bin/ 308157289 + app/ 354237 + models/ 1514788755, i.e. including the derived q4_0 model and excluding the f16 - and does not count logs/ or the staged uninstaller. Peak transient disk during that install is about 5.9 GB: the download cache plus the install tree while the f16 is briefly present.

archiveTools.tar.bz2: tar.exe -xjf  (bsdtar ships with Windows 10/11, no extra tooling needed)
archiveTools.none: Single file: copy to the extract target.

components.name: whisper.cpp
components.purpose: Speech recognition engine. OpenBLAS CPU build - no CUDA, no GPU required.

extract.note: Derives the DEFAULT speech model at install time from the f16 weights - see derivedComponents[]. It comes out of THIS archive, the same already-SHA-256-verified zip as whisper-cli.exe, so vendoring it adds no new download, no new upstream, and no new provenance question. 111616 bytes. Usage: whisper-quantize.exe <model-f16.bin> <model-quant.bin> q4_0.
All CPU variants: the ggml loader picks the best match for the host CPU at runtime, so shipping only one would break other machines.

components.name: ffmpeg
components.purpose: Probes media metadata (ffprobe) and decodes any container to 16 kHz mono PCM WAV (ffmpeg). Decode only - no encoders are used.
components.licenseVerifiedFrom: LICENSE.txt bundled in the archive is LGPL v3; ffmpeg -version shows no --enable-gpl and no --enable-nonfree, and --enable-version3 is present.
components.licenseNote: LGPL variant chosen deliberately over the GPLv3 gyan.dev and BtbN GPL builds. TranscribeIt only decodes audio, so the GPL-only encoders (x264/x265) are not needed. Verified that aac, mp3, opus, flac, wmav2, alac and ac3 all decode, from mp4/m4a/mov/mkv/ogg/flac/asf/wav containers. BtbN build scripts are MIT; the ffmpeg binaries they produce are LGPLv3 here.

components.name: whisper-model-ggml-large-v3-turbo-q5_0
components.purpose: PREVIOUS default speech model, now the manual recovery path. large-v3-turbo quantised to q5_0. The DEFAULT is the q4_0 model derived at install time (see derivedComponents[]), which measured 1.39x faster on the transcription stage for an IDENTICAL 1.58% word error rate on the noisy fixture. This one is retained deliberately, not by inertia: it is the only large-v3-turbo variant that is actually HOSTED, so if the derivation ever fails on some future machine, setting transcription.model back to this filename in config.json gives a working install with nothing outside this manifest. There is no automatic fallback - that is a config edit, not engine behaviour.

components.name: whisper-model-ggml-large-v3-turbo-f16
components.purpose: INSTALL-TIME SOURCE ONLY - not a shipped artefact, and the one component in this manifest that is deliberately absent when the install finishes. These are the published f16 large-v3-turbo weights, from which the installer derives the DEFAULT q4_0 model locally (see derivedComponents[]) and then deletes them. The alternative was shipping a q4_0 file that exists on exactly one laptop and appears in no manifest, which is what this change removes. Cost of the honest version: +1.55 GiB of one-time download, and zero net installed footprint.
components.licenseVerifiedFrom: https://huggingface.co/api/models/ggerganov/whisper.cpp -> cardData.license = mit, gated = False. Upstream weights openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo are also MIT.
components.sha256VerifiedFrom: MEASURED 2026-08-27 from the file actually downloaded on this device (1624555275 bytes, streamed SHA-256), and cross-checked against lfs.oid in https://huggingface.co/api/models/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/tree/main?recursive=true. The two agree. Corroborated a third way: quantising this file reproduces the pinned q4_0 hash byte for byte, and that q4_0 was originally produced from an INDEPENDENT download of these weights - so both downloads were identical. components.name: whisper-model-ggml-base.en-q8_0
components.purpose: BEST-TIMESTAMPS speech model, and the fallback for the fast path. Backed the Send To entry 'Heresay - Fastest transcript (no speakers)' until 2026-08-27, when tiny.en-q8_0 took that role; kept because it is the most accurately TIMED model measured in this project - per-utterance onset error median 0.19 s, p90 0.39 s, max 0.65 s, better even than large-v3-turbo-q4_0 (max 1.48 s), because its shorter segments keep boundaries tight. Select it with transcription.model in config.json when timing matters more than speed. MEASURED 2026-08-27 on mains, 347.86 s fixture, WHOLE PIPELINE end to end: 68.21 s without diarization = 5.10x realtime, against under 1.45x for the default q4_0 entry, at 2.48% word error rate (one wrong word in 40 - essentially small.en's 2.37%). This is the first model in this project measured end to end rather than by stage ratio. NOTE the reason originally recorded here for preferring it over tiny.en - that 'these transcripts carry timestamps that get quoted verbatim' - was FALSE and was never checked with the requirements owner, who confirmed on 2026-08-27 that approximate timestamps are acceptable for the intended use. The genuine timestamp difference is real but small in the median and shows up as a single outlier; see the tiny.en-q8_0 entry. Required, not optional: it remains a manifest component so the fallback is always present rather than needing a download at the moment someone needs it.

derivedComponents.name: whisper-model-ggml-large-v3-turbo-q4_0
derivedComponents.purpose: DEFAULT speech model. large-v3-turbo quantised to q4_0. MEASURED 1.39x faster than the q5_0 it replaced on the transcription stage for an IDENTICAL 1.58% word error rate on the noisy fixture. The 0.34-point penalty q4_0 shows on clean audio disappears under noise, which is the case that matters.
derivedComponents.whyDerived: It does not exist upstream. There is NO q4_0 file anywhere in huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp - confirmed 2026-08-27 against the repository tree API, zero matches for q4_0 - and every other hosted q4_0 variant that was tried returned 404. So the choice is between shipping a file that exists only because someone once ran an unvendored tool on one laptop, or deriving it here from published weights with a vendored tool. This is the second. It is the difference between an installer that works on one machine and an installer that works.
derivedComponents.licenseNote: Quantisation is a lossy numeric transform of the f16 weights and creates no new licensable work. The MIT terms of the upstream openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo weights carry through unchanged.
derivedComponents.reproducibility: MEASURED REPRODUCIBLE on this device, 2026-08-27. Two consecutive derivations from the same f16 input produced byte-identical output (473992235 bytes, SHA-256 2ceb779c...2155), and both matched a third copy that had been produced weeks earlier from an INDEPENDENT download of the f16 weights. Derivation cost 8-13 s of CPU, so it is noise against a 1.55 GiB download.
derivedComponents.verificationPolicy: sizeBytes is a HARD gate - the quantised size is fixed by the tensor shapes and the quant type, so it cannot legitimately vary, and a mismatch aborts the install. sha256 is compared and reported but is NOT a hard gate. Reason: whisper-quantize loads whichever ggml-cpu-*.dll matches the host CPU, so bit-identical output on a different microarchitecture is likely but not guaranteed, and a check that fails on every install of some future machine would be worse than no check at all - it would break exactly the clean-install case this whole component exists to fix. A mismatch is therefore a loud warning, the actual hash is recorded in install-manifest.json, and the artefact is still trusted because BOTH of its inputs were SHA-256 verified against this manifest: the f16 weights and the quantiser binary's containing archive. Provenance does not depend on the output hash matching.
derivedComponents.installerNote: Runs after all downloads and before install-manifest.json is written. Idempotent: an existing correct q4_0 suppresses both the derivation AND the 1.55 GiB f16 download, so a re-run costs one hash of the existing file. Recorded in install-manifest.json under files[] so uninstall removes it, and under derivedModels[] with its measured hash, its inputs, and whether it matched this pinned value.
